title: System Freezes Completely After Resume From Sleep – KDE Plasma
body: I've now reinstalled Arch Linux from scratch five times trying to isolate a persistent issue, and I still can't pin it down. Every time I set up Arch from the ISO, follow the installation guide closely, and install KDE Plasma with plasma-meta, kde-applications, and sddm, the system seems to work fine until I suspend to RAM (sleep) and then try to resume. System Specs: -i5 11357-G with dual graphics: -Intel integrated GPU -NVIDIA GeForce MX330 (2GB) Its a dual boot, but arch is ona complete separate ssd Currently using only the Intel graphics (no NVIDIA drivers installed) on the latest install (fifth attempt) Desktop environment: KDE Plasma Kernel: linux Bootloader: GRUB (EFI) Issue: After waking up the laptop from sleep, I can log in, but 20–30 seconds later, the system completely freezes. No mouse movement, no keyboard input, no cursor — nothing. Caps Lock doesn’t toggle, so I suspect a hard kernel freeze. Only option: hard reboot using the power button. Upon reboot, journalctl -b -1 shows a few errors, sometimes related to: i2c_hid_acpi ath10k_pci kwin wayland crash etc etc If anyone has faced a similar freeze only after resume, or knows how to definitively trace such hard freezes, I’d really appreciate help.
